name: Clement Mitchell
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember scraping starch out of my first cook's collar.” On Sunday, near Lighthouse Cove, Clement takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I can't stand a starched collar since catering school. I asked for one shirt to be ironed differently.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a cream pullover and a watch on a cracked leather band. Clement has fine brows over wide-set eyes, with short black hair swept back. Clement holds eye contact until the other person has finished during a conversation.
personality: Clement takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Clement can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To order one shirt without starch.
family: Reina Gallagher is Clement’s cousin. Clement calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Reina leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *Rent in a biscuit tin*, Reina says, “I collected rent in the rain and swapped the tins.”
connections: Anton Wong. A secret laundry mark tells the cook who can leave the collar unstarched.

reactions.situation: An elderly tenant wants to iron the collar personally
reactions.response: Clement lets the tenant do the collar at a safe height and takes the heavier laundry.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Clement asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.
